I couldn't do this research. The search-and-fetch tool turned down my first request because its usage limit for this turn had already been reached, so I didn't get to open any pages.

That means I have no source pages to work from. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes from memory.

**What I'd read once the tool works again:**
- **Verse-by-verse commentaries:** Enduring Word on Psalm 96; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com; and the Psalm 96 page on preceptaustin.org.
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon on this psalm (spurgeon.org or ccel.org), Calvin's commentary (ccel.org), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org).
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes, especially on v. 9 ("splendor of His holiness") and v. 10 ("The LORD reigns").
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine on this psalm at newadvent.org (numbered Psalm 95 in older Catholic Bibles). I'd also check whether any approved site discusses the old Christian reading of v. 10 as "the Lord reigned from the tree."

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start on these pages and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point.
